facts.label: The Two Spirits
facts.fact: Zoroaster framed creation as a primal choice between two spirits — one bounteous, one destructive — who at the beginning chose life and truth, or the Lie.

facts.label: The Lie
facts.fact: Against the wholly good Ahura Mazda stands Angra Mainyu, the principle of the Lie (druj) — destruction and death set opposite order and truth.

facts.label: Yang, the bright line
facts.fact: In the Chinese hexagrams an unbroken line stands for yang — the active, bright principle — the paired opposite of yin.

facts.label: Yin, the broken line
facts.fact: A broken line stands for yin — the receptive, dark principle — stacked with yang into the sixty-four figures of the Yijing.

facts.label: The Feather of Ma'at
facts.fact: In the Egyptian judgment the heart is weighed against the feather of Ma'at — truth, order, and justice — against which the disorder of Isfet is measured.

facts.label: Horus and Set
facts.fact: Egypt's great contest pits Horus, who grows up to avenge his father Osiris, against Set — order reclaiming the throne from chaos.
